findings.title: Map-role checks ignore manage-clients admins
findings.body: canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles only call hasPermission and never root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS) or canManage(client). When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is on, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() always returns this class, so realm admins who only have the manage-clients role are denied mapping client roles, composite roles, and client-scope roles unless a separate FGAP policy exists. Those operations 403 for users who are allowed to manage the client.

findings.title: Missing all-clients resource causes NPE
findings.body: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource when no per-client resource exists, then immediately calls PolicyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and later evaluatePermission without a null check. getResourceTypeResource returns null when the "Clients" resource was never created (see init() early return on an existing admin-permissions client). A view/manage/configure check then throws NullPointerException instead of returning false, so admin API calls 500 rather than 403.

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions client is not migrated
findings.body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already set and never adds the new Clients resource type or the configure, map-roles-client-scope, and map-roles-composite scopes. Realms that initialized FGAP V2 when only Users existed keep the old resource server. Creating or evaluating a Clients permission then fails in getScope with "Scope [configure] does not exist" (or the equivalent for the other new scopes), so the feature does not work after upgrade.

findings.title: Per-client resources are created without a type
findings.body: getOrCreateResource creates the client resource with resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, owner) and only updateScopes. It never sets the resource type to CLIENTS, unlike init() which calls resource.setType(type) for the all-clients resource. ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission lists candidates with resourceStore.findByType(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE). Per-client grants are therefore omitted from that set, so admin list/filter paths that rely on getClientsWithPermission drop clients the caller is actually allowed to see. The same query can also include the all-clients resource whose name is the literal "Clients", which is not a client id.

findings.title: Client resource names are not resolved
findings.body: getResourceName only special-cases the Users resource type. Client resources are stored under the internal client id and typically have a null display name, so the method returns null (or a blank display name) for Clients policies. Admin permission APIs and the console therefore show an empty resource name instead of the clientId for client-scoped permissions.

findings.title: V2 client permission methods throw instead of denying
findings.body: canExchangeTo, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, and the permission-policy accessors throw UnsupportedOperationException. With the V2 feature enabled, every clients() call uses this class. Token-exchange checks and the client management-permissions admin endpoints therefore 500 instead of returning false or a disabled permissions representation. The removal listener was gated to the V1 feature, but these other callers were not.
